subject: reading
title: The Loud Sound
about: A thump in the dark turns out to be Boots the cat. Adds the Unit 3 sounds: oo (moon, Boots, book, foot, too), ou (Scout, loud, sound), oi (points) and aw (yawns), with ee (creep) and magic e (late), plus the tricky words what, he, you, are, down and of. Decodable at CKLA Unit 3, so he can read it alone.
tip: Cold read first, then read it to him, then let him read it again, making each Thump a little louder.

passage.text:
It is late.
The moon is up.
Beth is in bed.
Scout is snug at the foot of the bed.

Thump!
Beth sits up.
"What is that loud sound?"
Scout sniffs.
Thump! Thump!

Beth and Scout creep down the steps.
Beth points at the den.
It is Boots the cat!
Boots is up on a shelf.
He bats a book.
Thump!
It hits the rug.

Beth grins.
"Boots, you are too loud!" says Beth.
Scout wags.
Boots just yawns.

cards.q: Who is in bed when the story starts?
cards.note: Beth is in bed, with Scout snug at the foot of it.
Beth points at the den, and the sound is in there.
Boots bats a book off a shelf and it thumps on the rug.

cards.q: What does Boots do on the shelf?
cards.note: He bats a book and it hits the rug with a thump.
The story starts with Beth in bed; the wag and the yawn come at the end.

cards.q: What does Boots do at the end?
cards.note: The last line is Boots just yawns.

cards.q: How does Beth feel when she sees it is Boots?
cards.note: Beth grins, so she is glad.

cards.q: Why do Beth and Scout creep down the steps?
cards.note: They go to find out what is making the loud sound.
A loud sound is a big, booming one; a thump in a quiet house is loud.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Moon is in the story; mood and noon are look-alikes that are not.
